Zazzaroni difende Allegri: "In un mondo in cui tutti si vendono, Max preferisce restare sé stesso"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, non un'assoluzione per gli errori commessi, ma una difesa dell'uomo e dell'allenatore.
  • “Si fa presto a essere Allegri, ma non è poi così semplice.
  • Industry observers note that “In un mondo in cui tutti si vendono, Max preferisce restare sé stesso.

According to recent reports, non un'assoluzione per gli errori commessi, ma una difesa dell'uomo e dell'allenatore. Nel suo editoriale sulle colonne del Corriere dello Sport, il direttore Ivan Zazzaroni ripercorre le scelte professionali di Massimiliano Allegri, oggi alle prese con le difficoltà del Napoli: “Di errori e di scelte in questi anni Max ne ha fatti tanti perché non sbaglia solo chi sta fermo, ogni decisione ha il proprio lato oscuro e Max non è il tipo a cui puoi semplicemente mettere un assegno in bianco davanti agli occhi”.

“Si fa presto a essere Allegri, ma non è poi così semplice. Non lo è in particolare da qualche anno, precisamente da quando - scelta imperdonabile - rinunciò al contratto col Real Madrid, la società più importante al mondo (tre anni a 8,5 milioni netti a stagione più i premi) per tornare in una Juve che di lì a poco si sarebbe sfasciata sotto i colpi assestati dall’interno (Elkann-Agnelli), dalla Procura di Torino e dalla giustizia sportiva. Non è semplice, se hai il carattere di Max, tacere dopo aver ascoltato o letto certe intemerate social, attacchi personali d’ogni genere, le offese dei nemichetti like to like, le ossessive stupidaggini dei tanti imitatori di Adani e Cassano, i pifferai dell’antiallegrismo forse più per marketing che per reale convinzione”.

Industry observers note that “In un mondo in cui tutti si vendono, Max preferisce restare sé stesso. Anche se non è semplice subire in silenzio, anche se è complicato non rispondere a chiunque, come faceva da ragazzo a Livorno o da calciatore poco incline a tacere. Non è semplice, ma significa essere diventati adulti. Nel parco giochi sono rimasti gli altri e Max è diventato grande anche quando gli è capitato di cadere. Uscire da un Milan che nella seconda parte della stagione aveva dilapidato un autentico patrimonio di punti e denari - una sua responsabilità, ci mancherebbe - lo ha messo sul banco degli imputati, ma anche se Allegri non ha mai chiesto difese d’ufficio è utile ricordare che la società aveva del tutto disatteso le sue indicazioni di mercato. 'Non ci sono soldi per il difensore e l’attaccante', la risposta alle richieste, salvo poi vedere che lo stesso difensore e soprattutto lo stesso attaccante mesi dopo è stato pagato 74 milioni”.

Latest Update: Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery.

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'.

According to recent reports, it's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

The treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly.

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday.

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their new training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

Sources indicate that it’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is remarked to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.

Manca ancora l'ufficialità, ma non sembrano esserci più dubbi: al termine della stagione Nico Paz lascerà il Como e farà ritorno al Real Madrid. Secondo quanto afferma COPE, il club merengue eserciterà la sua opzione di riacquisto e riporterà alla base il fantasista argentino dopo tre anni trascorsi in riva al lago.

Recent findings suggest that la scorsa estate, come noto, il Real Madrid ha ceduto al Como il 50% dei diritti su Nico Paz per 60 milioni di euro, portando la valutazione complessiva del calciatore a 120 milioni di euro. In precedenza, nel 2024, il club lariano aveva già versato 6 milioni di euro per assicurarsi il talentuoso classe 2004. Su precisa richiesta del diretto interessato, il Real Madrid ha acconsentito al suo desiderio di rimanere in Italia per un'ulteriore stagione, così da proseguire il suo percorso di crescita e maturazione. ponendo però una condizione che permettesse un suo ritorno in Spagna: una clausola da 80 milioni di euro, che la società madrilena intende ora attivare all'apertura della prossima finestra di mercato estiva.

In a recent development, dopo tanti anni, Antonio Conte rivela i motivi che lo hanno spinto a dire addio all'Inter nell'estate del 2021. E lo fa nel corso dell'intervista concessa a Cronache di Spogliatoio, che uscirà integralmente nella giornata di domani, ma che in un estratto riporta le dichiarazioni dell'ex allenatore nerazzurro sul suo arrivo a Milano e sulla separazione dopo la vittoria dello scudetto. Ecco le sue parole, a partire dal rapporto con Lukaku:.

It has been revealed that "Lukaku non era abituato a giocare spalle alla porta, quindi aveva solo una fase, quella della ripartenza. Per le caratteristiche che aveva lui, per il tipo di giocatore che era, doveva diventare per forza completo. Mi ricordo che i primi tempi veniva e mi diceva: 'Mister, però io non sono portato a tenere palla in area, tenere botta, io devo prendere e attaccare'. Io gli ho detto: 'Romelu, tu devi diventare un giocatore completo'. Ricordo che con Paolo Vanoli, che era nel mio staff e ora è allenatore della Fiorentina, prendevamo Romelu e lo allenavamo con lo sparapalloni, che sparava forte e lui doveva proteggere palla con Vanoli che gli arrivava da dietro e lo contrastava. E' diventato Lukaku per quello, perché ti riesce a fare entrambe le cose: quando c'è da attaccare la profondità, ha gamba, forza e velocità per farlo; quando c'è da tenere botta e te lo porti in area, è come portarti il gol in casa, perché ti fa sponda e ti fa fare gol".

"Marotta e Zhang vengono e mi dicono: 'Noi vogliamo che tu ci riporti alla vittoria. Non vinciamo da 10 anni, vogliamo interrompere in Italia l'egemonia della Juventus e poi farci onore anche all'estero. Un obiettivo chiaro da parte della società, con cui fare un percorso insieme. Inevitabile che, se stiamo andando in una direzione, poi dobbiamo andare lì, anche perché tu mi hai chiesto qualcosa. Io vado dall'Inter per quale motivo? Abbiamo appena vinto lo scudetto: facciamo una riunione in cui mi viene detto che praticamente tutti i calciatori potevano essere venduti. I patti prima erano: costruiamo, buttiamo giù l'egemonia della Juventus e poi creiamo una struttura che possa durare negli anni e diventiamo più competitivi nel corso degli anni anche in Europa. Le condizioni cambiate dalla Cina? Sì, ma comunque quando tu ti impegni con un club, ti impegni con un popolo, con un tifoso".

In a recent development, eli Junior Kroupi non aveva bisogno della Nazionale francese per farsi conoscere. Il classe 2006, però, ha ulteriormente acceso i riflettori su di sé con un debutto da protagonista con i Bleus, impreziosito dal gol decisivo contro la Turchia. Secondo quanto riportato da The Athletic, tra i club interessati al giovane attaccante del Bournemouth ci sarebbe anche il Paris Saint-Germain, pronto a valutare un investimento per la prossima estate.

Kroupi, arrivato al Bournemouth dal Lorient nel 2025 e legato al club inglese fino al 2030, ha vissuto una prima stagione in Premier League da protagonista con 13 gol in 33 presenze. Il suo rendimento ha attirato anche il Barcellona e il futuro del giocatore potrebbe essere lontano dall'Inghilterra.

In Francia c'è chi spinge per un ritorno in patria e proprio il PSG potrebbe essere la destinazione ideale: "Non bisogna lasciarselo scappare", dicono i media, ricordando come il club parigino stia cercando di costruire una squadra sempre più francese.

Un dettaglio che potrebbe favorire l'affare è anche il legame con l'agente Moussa Sissoko, che cura gli interessi di giocatori già presenti nella rosa come Désiré Doué, Dembélé e Kvaratskhelia. Dopo l'impatto con la Francia di Zinedine Zidane, Kroupi sembra aver già conquistato un posto nel futuro dei Bleus. E forse anche quello del PSG.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

In a recent development, so much for the fresh group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

Recent findings suggest that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

Industry observers note that city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a latest City, different personnel and even a new look.

Sources indicate that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

According to recent reports, phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Sources indicate that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This highlights how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

Industry observers note that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he highlighted why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland remarked. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

It has been revealed that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

It has been revealed that 36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

Industry observers note that “I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a newly introduced step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

It has been revealed that “Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

According to recent reports, “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

It has been revealed that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

There will be five added minutes.

According to recent reports, that is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

According to recent reports, haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

It has been revealed that whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

Recent findings suggest that that is a massive chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

In a recent development, manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

Sources indicate that A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

In a recent development, enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Sources indicate that porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Sources indicate that varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

It has been revealed that donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT.

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

Industry observers note that we are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

In a recent development, gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee indicates the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

Recent findings suggest that D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

According to recent reports, manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” mentioned Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that highlights a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Industry observers note that porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Sources indicate that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

According to recent reports, L’Atalanta di questo inizio ciclo con Maurizio Sarri sta stentando. Per gioco e per risultati. Fino a questo momento la società ha sempre difeso e portato avanti la scelta estiva, ben consapevole del tempo e delle difficoltà che un cambiamento tale di filosofia si sarebbe portato dietro. Avanti con Sarri a prescindere dai risultati quindi, anche se alla fine sono sempre loro a dare i giudizi finali. Prima della sosta, pur senza brillare, la Dea ha trovato 3 punti importantissimi col Monza e ora alla ripresa c’è la sfida contro l’Inter.

It has been revealed that da una parte sono evidenti le difficoltà. Dall’altra l’occasione è ghiotta per provare dare continuità di punti e di entusiasmo: è chiaro che un successo contro l’Inter darebbe slancio a Krstovic e compagni anche per le prossime settimane. Per provare a gettare il cuore oltre l’ostacolo, però, la Dea dovrà abbattere anche un blocco psicologico che si è formato negli ultimi anni prima con Gasperini e poi con Palladino. E ora Sarri ha l’occasione per provare ad invertire la rotta.

Recent findings suggest that in Serie A l’Inter è diventata una bestia nera per l’Atalanta. I bergamaschi infatti non ottengono un successo contro i campioni d’Italia in carica addirittura da 15 partite. Un periodo lunghissimo in cui sono arrivate 9 sconfitte, 6 pareggi e appunto nessuna vittoria. 6 punti raccolti su 45 disponibili. Evidente come al di là del divario tecnico esista una sorta di pressione psicologica che negli anni ha lasciato la Dea a bocca asciutta. Anche per questo, la sfida di domenica sera sembra avere un po’ più di peso rispetto al solito.

Published: 06:41 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 13 November 2026.

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

In a recent development, in his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'.

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi.

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro.

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'.

The French then went onto say: 'The most important thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'.

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'.

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

#2843. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5475 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • According to recent reports, so, earn it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

According to recent reports, so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face noted it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Sources indicate that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

According to recent reports, mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ latest head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Recent findings suggest that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A massive European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola noted, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo demonstrated he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

According to recent reports, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

In a recent development, it owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Recent findings suggest that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

Industry observers note that the Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a upcoming contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

Recent findings suggest that “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a major responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

It has been revealed that atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone stated. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Un gesto di solidarietà che può fare la differenza.
  • All’evento parteciperà anche Patrizio Oliva, campione olimpico di pugilato e testimonial di Union, che incontrerà i partecipanti e sosterrà la campagna di sensibilizzazione.
  • According to recent reports, I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Un gesto di solidarietà che può fare la differenza. Sabato 21 novembre, dalle 9 alle 13, il Center Union di Aversa, in Viale Kennedy 35, ospiterà “Dona, fai la differenza”, iniziativa promossa da Union Gas e Luce in collaborazione con la Casa del Donatore di Aversa per sensibilizzare sull’importanza della donazione del sangue.

All’evento parteciperà anche Patrizio Oliva, campione olimpico di pugilato e testimonial di Union, che incontrerà i partecipanti e sosterrà la campagna di sensibilizzazione. «Non serve essere campioni per fare un gesto da campioni», è il messaggio lanciato dall’ex pugile. L’iniziativa si inserisce nell’impegno di Union a favore del territorio e della responsabilità sociale, con l’obiettivo di coinvolgere cittadini, associazioni e realtà locali nella promozione della cultura della donazione. «L’energia più bella è quella che condividiamo», il messaggio che accompagna l’evento.

Sources indicate that un nome chiacchieratissimo, dopo le ultime prestazioni specie con le giovanili della nazionale italiana, quello di Emanuele Rao, esterno offensivo sinistro di proprietà del Napoli ma ora in prestito al Pisa, in Serie B. Giocate e gol di pregevoli fattura lo hanno portato alla ribalta, e il poco spazio che sta trovando in Toscana ha già acceso il mercato, in vista poi di gennaio.

It has been revealed that proprio nel corso della conferenza stampa di ieri, che anticipa il match contro l'Empoli, Paolo Bianco è stato molto chiaro sul calciatore: "Rao è fino a giugno un giocatore del Pisa, lo paga il Pisa che si è assicurato le sue prestazioni, per altro importanti. Emanuele ha la mia grandissima stima, e mi viene da sorridere perché dopo Avellino in tanti dicevano che può solo subentrare, ora, che ha fatto un eurogol in Nazionale, viene definito come uno che deve partire sempre titolare: da un giorno all'altro cambia tutto. Abbiamo un solo problema: davanti a lui c'è un giocatore forte come Tramoni, che ha una caratteristica differente, è tatticamente più intelligente e dà un equilibrio diverso. Poi, è vero che Rao può giocare anche in un altro ruolo, ci sono tanti pensieri su di lui". Chiaro e conciso il tecnico del Pisa, che ha spiegato perfettamente quella che è la situazione. Il Pisa ha un reparto avanzo molto ricco e completo, non è quello che va sistemato in casa nerazzurra, e viene difficile adesso variare gli elementi, soprattutto per quello che si vede in campo. Rao è un giocatore fortissimo, lo ha detto e ribadito anche Bianco, ma è a oggi meno funzionale rispetto ad altri nella chiave tattica che il citato trainer vuole; ciò, non significa che non veda il classe 2006, che nelle rotazioni è poi un elemento principe.

La situazione creatasi, però, sembra non esser particolarmente gradita al Napoli, che, come rimbalza dalla Campania, starebbe pensando di riprendere il giocatore a gennaio. Anche su chiara indicazioni di Massimiliano Allegri. Al netto delle considerazioni che si possono fare sul futuro del trainer in azzurro - sarà ancora lui l'allenatore dei partenopei a gennaio? -, c'è però la questione legata all'accordo tra i club: i campani, comunque, sarebbero disposti a dare una sorta di indennizzo al Pisa se effettivamente si concludesse anticipatamente il prestito.

Fisicità, rapidità, qualità tecniche, incisività negli ultimi metri, adattamento a più ruoli nel reparto avanzato, visione di gioco: tutte caratteristiche proprie di Rao. Ma da qui a dire che sia pronto per la Serie A, ce ne passa. Chiariamo: nessuno sta mettendo in dubbio il valore del giocatore, si evidenzia semplicemente il problema della gestione del talento in Italia. Troppo spesso, ci sono due estremi per i ragazzi giovani: o vengono tenuti in Primavera fino a 20 anni, o vengono bruciati per la fretta di inserirli, senza permettere loro di fare tutti gli step necessari. Camarda docet. Evitiamo, dunque, di bruciare un altro possibile elemento del futuro azzurro. Dove per azzurro, ovviamente, non si intende solo il Napoli.

#2838. Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1609 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • England will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions.
  • Sources indicate that it wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's significant night at Wembley against Croatia, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026.

England will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions. A win in Madrid could see Thomas Tuchel's team progress to the quarter-finals next March as group winners.

Sources indicate that it wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's significant night at Wembley against Croatia, though. Indeed this was probably England's worst performance since losing to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final last July.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the key concerns emerging from last night's tight squeeze.

Self-defeating abuse of White is madness and must stop.

In case nobody has noticed, England are not over stocked with competent right-backs.

It has been revealed that trent Alexander-Arnold isn't wholly trusted in substantial games by Thomas Tuchel, Reece James is always injured and Tino Livramento has also struggled to be available. Why, then, is a significant section of the England support so determined to drive Ben White away from the international scene?

In a recent development, white plays for Arsenal, the champions of England. He is a fine, versatile defender who would be gratefully received and appreciated by fans of most national teams in world football. He had issues with the previous England management regime and does not apologise for that.

It has been revealed that ben White was booed when he came on. The abuse towards the defender must stop.

He spoke about it this week and made it clear he didn't wish to reopen old wounds. All that matters now is that he is willing and available. But – despite a plea from Tuchel before this game – England fans still booed him when he came on as a substitute last night.

In a recent development, it's a disgraceful way to treat a footballer who can be an asset to his country going forwards and it's something the England manager cares deeply about. Do we want to win the next Euros or not? Do we want our best players motivated and driven and part of the squad? Or do we want to faff about harbouring old grudges related to a situation in Qatar four winters ago that none of us really know that much about?

According to recent reports, the choice is clear. If we are not careful, we will drive a good footballer away from the England set-up for good. It's madness.

Significant night for Kane but questions for England.

Sources indicate that they came to celebrate Harry Kane and the England captain got his goal. Number 92 for the striker. Beneath all the fuss over England's talisman, however, this came perilously close to being a step backwards for Thomas Tuchel's England.

Industry observers note that the England manager has been saying since the last international break in September and October that he wanted his team to go to Madrid on Sunday in with a shout at knocking Spain from the top of this Nations League Group. Had Croatia been a little smarter in front of goal at Wembley last night, England would have been heading for a dead rubber against the world champions.

Harry Kane scored on his substantial night as England edged out a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley.

It was a night to remember for Kane as he was honoured after receiving his record 126th cap.

Three times in the last ten minutes of this game, Croatia had good opportunities to score a second goal and take a point from the game that would have been perfectly justified. So England crawled over the line but there was little here that was impressive with questions emerging once again about how capable really are when they don't have the ball.

Kane put it well himself afterwards when he stated: 'You can't always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday.'.

Tuchel himself will perhaps have quiet concerns. One of the German's worries about this England team is that they sometimes struggle to take training performances on to the field and this was another case in point.

The ultimate target for this team is to win the home Euros in 2028 and the pressure will need handling in front of their own supporters if they are to do that. With that in mind, it's good to know that the FA are interested in hosting the finals of this Nations League competition next summer.

If England make it through next March's two-legged quarter-finals, they could do with some practice of playing high-stakes games at Wembley.

Asked last week on the day he revealed his squad whether Jordan Pickford was still his number one goalkeeper, Tuchel was unequivocal.

In a recent development, 'He is,' said Tuchel. 'But the competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And James Trafford will get regular starts now, that's what we wanted. They shared the matches last time. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.'.

Morgan Rogers impressed after opening the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour.

Jordan Pickford starting against Croatia could lead to James Trafford playing against Spain.

Industry observers note that with all this in mind, it was expected that Trafford would start this game with Pickford getting the gloves for the one that really matters in Spain on Sunday. That wasn't the case, so we wait with interest to see what the England manager does in Madrid.

What nobody really wants is for a return to the situation we had in the 1980s when Ron Greenwood used to rotate between the late Ray Clemence and last night's guest of honour Peter Shilton.

England's back four is the one area of this team that can look unconvincing – they did again last night - and the last thing they need is not to know who their goalkeeper is from one match to the next. Tuchel is going to have to make a decision.

Interesting that Tuchel chose to put Dan Burn into his team for this game, despite the Newcastle defender not being in the original squad.

In a recent development, with Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa both absent with injuries, Everton's Jarrod Branthwaite would have expected to play on the left of Jarell Quansah here. Instead, Burn leapfrogged him in the queue and maybe we should have paid more attention to something Tuchel stated the day before the game.

'Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,' remarked Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite clearly has a way to go before he's fully trusted to start by Thomas Tuchel.

Recent findings suggest that 'You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a significant voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe where they followed in a high press and to man-man. And of course he was with us at the World Cup so he is used a bit more to our style of play.'.

That's all very well and logical but – that being the case – why was Branthwaite chosen ahead of Burn in the original group of 25 last Friday? Burn, as it happened, had a very good game last night.

According to recent reports, tuchel talks always about the value of players being in camp. 'The train is leaving the station,' is one of the England manager's more memorable quotes of recent times. Players like Cole Palmer, for example, have learned to their cost that missing meet-ups with injuries can be costly.

Bukayo Saka is not in that category and has plenty of credit in the bank with the England manager. However, Tuchel's fondness for Morgan Rogers is well known and Saka's absence does give him a way of getting the Chelsea player into his team. Rogers may be a number ten at heart but he was effective once again here out on the right side.

Industry observers note that the 24-year-old was one of England's better players on a muted night against Croatia and he deserved his first half goal. He gives England a more direct, athletic dimension on the opposite flank to the more balletic offerings of Anthony Gordon. Food for thought for Tuchel at least as Saka continues his own battle against persistent injuries.

Bukayo Saka's long-term place in England's team could be under threat from Morgan Rogers.

United should have moved for Hall.

Industry observers note that newcastle United were pretty much an open door in the summer as they sold players left right and centre. Gordon to Barcelona to make sure the club was the right side of the financial guidelines and then Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal simply because the players made it known they wanted to go.

Strange, then, that Manchester United didn't make a proper move for left-back Lewis Hall. Admittedly this wasn't the most difficult match in which he will have ever played, but Hall was impressive once again.

Sources indicate that with Luke Shaw so injury prone, Hall pretty much has the left-back berth sewn up for England but it feels as though he now needs to make the next step in his club career. United retain a nominal interest but who knows what incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino may think? It's hard to work out why United didn't try harder to sign him last summer. He has subsequently signed a new contract at Newcastle, of course.

It has been revealed that sono passati 500 giorni dall'insediamento di Gian Piero Gasperini a Trigoria e la sua prima richiesta di mercato non è ancora stata soddisfatta: un esterno offensivo dotato di velocità, capacità di strappo, forza fisica e gol. Durante l'estate Tony D'Amico ha avviato almeno 17 trattative, andando oltre i semplici sondaggi. Da Greenwood a Summerville, passando per Nusa, Leweling e Luiz Henrique. Nessuna è andata a buon fine, ma il direttore sportivo giallorosso continua a lavorare per accontentare il tecnico.

According to recent reports, come riportato dal Corriere dello Sport, uno dei profili seguiti è quello di Ruben van Bommel, ventiduenne del PSV Eindhoven e figlio dell'ex centrocampista di Milan e Bayern Monaco. Esterno sinistro di piede destro, alto 192 centimetri, l'olandese risponde alle caratteristiche richieste da Gasperini, ma la sua valutazione potrebbe già sfiorare i 40 milioni di euro. Più contenuti i costi di Derry Scherhant, talento del Friburgo che in questa stagione ha collezionato tre gol e otto assist in 917 minuti.

D'Amico segue con attenzione anche Jamie Bynoe-Gittens e Callum Hudson-Odoi, rispettivamente in uscita da Chelsea e Nottingham Forest. Per questi ultimi sarebbe più percorribile la strada del prestito con diritto di riscatto condizionato alla qualificazione in Champions League, la formula ideale per la Roma. Per gli altri obiettivi, invece, servirebbe un investimento importante: almeno 35 milioni di euro, la cifra che i Friedkin erano pronti a spendere a fine agosto per Leweling o Luiz Henrique.

Il centrocampista classe 2011 è stato impiegato da Rughetti in tutte le partite della stagione.

Recent findings suggest that andrea Morresi è il regista del centrocampo della Lazio di Rughetti. Secondo quanto riportato da Gazzetta Regionale, Il classe 2011, arrivato dal Perugia nell’estate del 2025, gioca davanti alla difesa ed è stato impiegato dal tecnico in tutte le partite di questa stagione. Nel derby con la Roma, un suo filtrante ha messo Coppola nelle condizioni di segnare il gol del momentaneo 2-1.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Morresi era approdato nella capitale nella passata stagione, entrando nell’Under 15. Si è preso presto le chiavi della mediana biancoceleste, interpretando il ruolo di playmaker anche nel campionato attuale. La sua presenza è un punto fermo nelle scelte di Rughetti.

Sources indicate that prima del passaggio al Perugia, Morresi è cresciuto nel settore giovanile della Treiese, dai Piccoli Amici ai Pulcini. L’arrivo alla Lazio nell’estate del 2025 ha aperto una nuova tappa del suo percorso: con la maglia biancoceleste ha trovato spazio stabilmente davanti alla difesa.

In quella posizione gestisce il pallone, distribuisce il gioco e cerca gli spazi per i compagni. Alla visione di gioco unisce tecnica e corsa nelle due fasi. Il suo destro si è già fatto notare anche sui calci di punizione, una soluzione con cui può rendersi decisivo.

Il suo contributo non si esaurisce però nella regia arretrata. Quando si apre la possibilità, Morresi avanza verso la trequarti avversaria. È dunque coinvolto sia nella costruzione delle azioni sia nel lavoro che precede le iniziative offensive della squadra.

According to recent reports, fino alla domenica del derby, la Lazio condivideva con la Roma l’imbattibilità in campionato. I biancocelesti si presentavano alla sfida con una struttura difensiva che li rendeva la seconda miglior difesa del raggruppamento. Anche il lavoro di Morresi davanti alla retroguardia contribuisce all’equilibrio della squadra.

In a recent development, contro i giallorossi, il numero 4 ha giocato in una zona di campo particolarmente affollata. Dall’altra parte c’era il miglior attacco del girone, capace di mettere alla prova la mediana biancoceleste. La Roma ha prevalso per 3-1 dopo aver dominato gran parte degli 80 minuti, ma nella ripresa la Lazio ha trovato la forza di reagire.

L’episodio che ha riaperto momentaneamente la partita è nato dai piedi di Morresi. Un suo passaggio filtrante ha raggiunto Coppola in posizione favorevole; il compagno ha poi mandato il pallone in rete per il 2-1. La speranza biancoceleste si è spenta con il terzo gol romanista, firmato da Abate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

It has been revealed that in casa Inter c'è una situazione non ancora scottante, ma che andrà affrontata quanto prima: il futuro di Marcus Thuram. L'attaccante francese sta vivendo una stagione da protagonista, ma il suo contratto scade il 30 giugno 2028, quando avrà 31 anni: scontata la volontà dei nerazzurri di trattenerlo a Milano, ma difficilmente si potrà imbastire una trattativa alle cifre attuali. Senza dimenticare l'esplosione di Esposito e la clausola rescissoria che permetterebbe all'Inter di far registrare una plusvalenza da record in caso di cessione di Thuram.

It has been revealed that la Gazzetta dello Sport prova a fare il punto della situazione: "Thuram ha chiesto più volte ai dirigenti, già nel periodo in cui il direttore sportivo era Piero Ausilio, se esistesse la volontà di proseguire il rapporto insieme. L'Inter ha ovviamente detto che sì, non c'erano dubbi sulle intenzioni e che ci sarebbe stato modo di parlare a tempo debito di un nuovo accordo. [...] Ma il problema di Marcus, classe '97, è proprio questo: quando scadrà il contratto attuale avrà già 31 anni. Come potrebbe la società proporgli oggi un'offerta al rialzo?".

"Thuram si aspetta di ottenere un aumento di stipendio rispetto ai 6 milioni netti (il decreto crescita aiuta nella tassazione il club) che gli vengono versati adesso. Solo che la politica della sostenibilità imposta da Oaktree ha stabilito che i nuovi contratti debbano prevedere una base fissa non altissima abbinata a una ricca parte mobile: in altre parole, i calciatori devono meritare i loro emolumenti attraverso bonus personali e collettivi determinati dal rendimento. [...] Thuram, per poter restare all'Inter come desidera, dovrà abbassare in modo considerevole le pretese".

In a recent development, "Dalla società filtra ottimismo, oltre alla determinazione di fissare dei paletti finanziari. Però la palla spetta all'interlocutore, di solito bravo a muoverla per gol e assist. Se non si dovesse raggiungere un'intesa, a giugno si potrebbero fare altri ragionamenti: in fondo nell'Inter e nella nazionale italiana si sta affermando un centravanti chiamato Pio Esposito che reclama spazio in attacco. E Thuram ha un certo appeal internazionale, tale da richiamare attenzioni che possono diventare interessamenti concreti: essendo stato ingaggiato a parametro zero, sarebbe una plusvalenza gustosa da valutare.

Piano però con le proiezioni, una postilla sul tema è doverosa: ogni anno, di questi tempi o anche più avanti nella stagione, si parla di possibili offerte per Thuram, che ha una clausola da 85 milioni mai neppure avvicinata da alcuno. E così Marcus è sempre rimasto felicemente a Milano. Anche stavolta la storia potrebbe finire così, magari con un contratto più lungo e meno pesante da ammortizzare per l'Inter".
