Latest Update: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5352 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the upcoming Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • It has been revealed that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
  • Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the upcoming Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

It has been revealed that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

Industry observers note that in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

In a recent development, their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

According to recent reports, “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” noted Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

Sources indicate that to lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

Industry observers note that in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” stated Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with latest arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:.

Possession: Napoli 42%-58% Arsenal.

Touches in opposition box: 9-52.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

It has been revealed that they kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Well that should have been that!

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Sources indicate that ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Industry observers note that martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

According to recent reports, there will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

According to recent reports, their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

Sources indicate that nuovo accordo in vista in casa Real Madrid. Federico Valverde, riportano i principali media spagnoli, ha raggiunto un'intesa con il club per prolungare il contratto fino al 2031, due anni in più rispetto all'attuale scadenza fissata al 2029. Un riconoscimento importante per il centrocampista uruguaiano, diventato nel tempo una delle figure più rappresentative dello spogliatoio e ora pronto a vivere un'altra lunga fase della sua avventura al Bernabéu.

Industry observers note that arrivato a Madrid a 18 anni dal Peñarol come una giovane promessa, Valverde ha conquistato spazio con lavoro e sacrificio, trasformandosi nel corso degli anni in un elemento imprescindibile. Il nuovo accordo non riguarda soltanto la durata del contratto, ma anche il suo peso all'interno della rosa: il classe 1998 sarà infatti uno dei giocatori più pagati della squadra, a conferma del nuovo status raggiunto. Il Real ha apprezzato soprattutto la sua capacità di adattarsi alle esigenze della squadra: con José Mourinho, Valverde ha spesso giocato anche da esterno, dimostrando grande disponibilità tattica. "Lo vedo come un giocatore importantissimo per la squadra. Il fatto che sia il capitano del Real Madrid gli dà una responsabilità diversa. Se necessario, potrà giocare anche da terzino sinistro", aveva spiegato il tecnico portoghese.

Recent findings suggest that valverde è il quarto giocatore più utilizzato da Mourinho in questa stagione e ha già inciso con tre gol e due assist. Ma il suo valore va oltre le statistiche: intensità, sacrificio e capacità di ricoprire più ruoli lo hanno reso un riferimento. A 28 anni, l'uruguaiano vanta già 14 trofei e 387 presenze con il Real Madrid, con 44 reti e 46 assist. Una crescita costruita passo dopo passo, dopo il passaggio dal Castilla e il prestito al Deportivo La Coruña prima del definitivo salto in prima squadra.

Published: 07:02 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:51 EST, 13 November 2026.

Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their fresh head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his latest job as United boss on Wednesday. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

There were no comments from Pochettino or United officials in Friday’s press release confirming his appointment because he remains contracted to US Soccer.

Pochettino remarked in the USMNT's statement: 'The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.'.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday, but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week.

United sources say that Pochettino’s experience, philosophy, personality and skill-set make him well suited for the job, as well as his record of developing individual talent and building excellent team cultures.

Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the Manchester United manager.

Michael Carrick was sacked after the club made their worst start to the season in 40 years.

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’.

Earlier in the week, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am on Thursday morning and was dismissed.

According to recent reports, he left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He became the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season.

United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

In a recent development, 'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

'His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'.

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick indicated.

United feel that the squad are far better than their position in the Premier League reveals.

They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

It has been a campaign in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and they are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league.

Pochettino's United travel to Anfield on November 22 before a Champions League clash at Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino's first home game against Brentford and then away match at Newcastle.

La lettera di Vanoli: "Fabregas mi ha insegnato la differenza tra il vincente e il perdente"

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that lunga lettera di Paolo Vanoli a Cronache di Spogliatoio.
  • Sources indicate that sull'insegnamento di Fabregas: "La differenza tra il vincente e il perdente è quello che si abbatte.
  • Industry observers note that su De Gea: "Lui è il mio capitano, oltre che essere il mio campione.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that lunga lettera di Paolo Vanoli a Cronache di Spogliatoio. Il tecnico della Fiorentina ha spiegato la sua decisione di tornare a guidare la Fiorentina per sostituire Fabio Grosso a inizio stagione, così come il doloroso addio arrivato in estate. Di seguito alcuni estratti, tra passato, presente e futuro.

Sources indicate that sull'insegnamento di Fabregas: "La differenza tra il vincente e il perdente è quello che si abbatte. Me lo ha insegnato Fàbregas, e l’ho portato come esempio ai miei ragazzi. (Quando lavoravo con Conte al Chelsea, ndr) mi aveva impressionato Fàbregas perché nel primo periodo non giocava tanto, ma in ogni allenamento ha voluto dimostrare a Conte che lui doveva giocare. Certo, sicuramente veniva arrabbiato al campo, gli dovevi stare lontano, ma non ha mollato un singolo giorno. E quando ha conquistato il posto, ha fatto vedere che le sue performance erano alte. Questo per me è un campione. Diversamente, uno che è un perdente si rassegna e trova alibi, e questi giocatori qua non hanno mai cercato alibi. Quindi non sapere accettare di stare in panchina ma combattere per la titolarità e io gli devo dare questa opportunità".

Industry observers note that su De Gea: "Lui è il mio capitano, oltre che essere il mio campione. Non penso che a una persona del suo calibro si debba insegnare come uscire dai momenti difficili. David è un grandissimo professionista, che nonostante l’età ha sempre fatto la differenza. Nella vita e nei percorsi, i periodi difficili possono capitare a tutti. Quando dico che è il mio capitano… basta questo: non penso che ci sia la necessità di spiegare a De Gea come uscire da un periodo negativo. Con i calciatori più esperti basta uno sguardo, ed è quello che accade con lui".

Su Parisi: "Quando a un calciatore chiedi uno sforzo, o un cambiamento, in un momento di difficoltà, e la risposta è 'Mister, nessun problema', allora vi assicuro che puoi andare a fare quello che vuoi. Fabiano è un esempio importante: una persona che ha sempre fatto il terzino, si è messo a disposizione quando la coperta era corta dicendo 'Se pensa che questo per la squadra vada bene, allora va bene. Non si preoccupi che io ci sono'. Capisci la persona che hai davanti. Disponibilità. Poi per la stagione che ha fatto dopo… forse ci eravamo sbagliati tutti pensando che fosse un terzino!".

It has been revealed that su Goncalves: "Vale la stessa cosa quest’anno con Pedro Goncalves: 'Mister, anche solo per 5 minuti, ma io ci sono'. Allora capisci che stai costruendo qualcosa, che davanti a questa possibilità di crescita e lavoro, puoi andare in battaglia".

According to recent reports, sulla salvezza dello scorso anno. "Ed è quello che ho fatto lo scorso anno. Quando mi hanno chiamato per salvare la Fiorentina: ho segnato il gol dell’ultimo trofeo nella storia di questo Club, si avvicinava il centenario della società… non potevo permetterlo. Dovevo portare i nostri tifosi fuori da questa situazione. E la chiarezza è quella che ho utilizzato il primo giorno. In quel momento, nonostante altre squadre, io volevo fortemente la Fiorentina. Ma fin quando non entri in un posto, non puoi sapere davvero quali siano i problemi reali. Come ho detto, abbiamo fatto un’impresa. Eravamo ultimi. Nessuno si era mai salvato senza aver mai vinto le prime 15 giornate".

In a recent development, su come ha lavorato l'anno scorso: "La prima cosa che ho fatto è togliere dalla testa dei giocatori la classica frase: 'Eh ma tanto siamo forti, ci salviamo'. Ho visto tante squadre, compresa la Fiorentina di Batistuta, retrocedere. La mia unica preoccupazione era togliere velocemente questa frase dall’ambiente. In più era scomparso il presidente Commisso, la situazione aveva diverse sfaccettature negative. A volte il compito di un allenatore è intervenire in maniera drastica e feroce sui problemi. Senza dimenticarci che nel mezzo c’era anche la Conference League, che ci ha creato un problema di liste dopo aver cambiato diversi calciatori a gennaio, e che io volevo vincere: se avessimo passato lo scoglio Crystal Palace, avremmo potuto farcela".

Sulle scelte difficili: "Lo scorso anno abbiamo dovuto fare scelte difficili. Come togliere la fascia di capitano a Ranieri. In quei momenti parli con i ragazzi, non devi giustificarti ma solo spiegare in modo trasparente il perché. Sono sicuro che Luca inizialmente abbia sofferto. O lo stesso Fagioli, che tutti dicevano che il play non poteva farlo: per me nel calcio moderno si può fare tutto, basta avere la mentalità. È arrivato in Nazionale da play, ma non è che adesso nei momenti di difficoltà bisogna rifugiarsi nel fatto che nasce mezzala".

Sulla scorsa travagliata estate: "Quest’estate mia moglie mi ha detto: 'Hai fatto un’estate… sembra che sia l’ultimo giorno prima che devi morire!'. Ho sofferto molto l’addio alla Fiorentina. Il tributo del Franchi dopo l’ultima partita mi aveva fatto capire che avevano riconosciuto i miei valori in quella difficoltà. Sono andato in Sardegna, ho provato a staccare. Ho avuto una forte delusione per qualcosa che mi ero meritato sul campo. Ma allo stesso tempo quando cambiano le società ed entrano persone nuove, è normale che le scelte societarie vadano accettate. E per quanto ci stessi male, l’ho sempre accettato".

It has been revealed that sul ritorno alla Fiorentina: "Sono venuto qui perché credo in questo nuovo progetto che la proprietà e il direttore stanno costruendo. Con una differenza: mi sono promesso di vivere di più Firenze. Nella scorsa stagione, per forza di cose, mi sono chiuso dentro al Viola Park: vivevo qui. Ma ne avevo bisogno. Avevo capito che per fare quello che abbiamo fatto, la mia residenza doveva essere al centro sportivo. Ora voglio godermela di più: ci sono stato da calciatore e so quanto sia incredibile. Sono andato alla prima del film di Pieraccioni, poi insieme ai nostri dottori a vedere il film di Bove che mi ha toccato tantissimo… ho preso casa, sto iniziando a girare. I tifosi sono molto affettuosi, anche se mi ricordano sempre le sostituzioni che faccio! Ma d’altronde si sa: gli italiani sono un popolo di allenatori. In particolar modo i fiorentini, che sono persone emotive ed empatiche proprio come me".

In a recent development, su Mastantuono: "Guardate Mastantuono: a 16 anni viveva già la pressione del River, poi è andato al Real Madrid. E non è un caso che il Real abbia pagato 60 milioni per prenderlo. Basta vedere il suo abbraccio dopo il Como, uscendo da un momento difficile. La sintonia, il fuoco argentino… è del 2007, ma dopo la tripletta segnata contro il Venezia in cui tutto il mondo parlava di lui, è andato a fare l’intervista post-partita dicendo in diretta che il premio del miglior giocatore della partita lo meritava Fagioli. Mentalità, una grandezza nonostante l’età. Franco deve completarsi, ma la scelta di venire a Firenze, che ha voluto lui, parla da sola nell’ottica di fare un salto in avanti".

Recent findings suggest that sul futuro di Mastantuono: "Su di lui posso solo dire: godiamocelo. Facciamolo crescere e godiamocelo. È una fortuna poter lavorare con un talento così. Ma come gli ho detto, il talento non basta: se si coccola solo del talento, prima o poi si ferma. Ma lui lo sa benissimo. Mi ha stupito la sua gestione della pressione. Ha una passione sfrenata per il calcio, lo vedi che gli piace proprio giocarlo. Ne parla, lo vede. Deve imparare però a capire quando dribblare e quando invece giocare più a due tocchi per la squadra. Fa parte dell’entusiasmo di un giocatore che vuole incidere. Ma meglio così: a questi giovani dico che devono osare. Come con la Juventus. Alla fine è la voglia di voler provare a vincere".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:48 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 08:08 EST, 13 November 2026.

Michael Carrick has released his first public statement on his Manchester United sacking, calling the job an 'immense privilege' in a classy 411-word tribute to the club's supporters.

The statement, released a little over 24 hours after his dismissal was confirmed, read: 'Dear United Fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

'There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

'With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else.

'Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

It has been revealed that 'It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

Michael Carrick has broken his silence on his sacking by Manchester United.

'We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

'I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

It has been revealed that 'That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

'A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

Recent findings suggest that 'To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

'And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead.

Recent findings suggest that 'I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a massive part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

In a recent development, 'I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on. Michael.'.

The statement follows his former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that Carrick had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of the United legend.

Carrick was left in the lurch by the club's hierarchy - but continued to attend training on Tuesday and Wednesday – amid widespread reports that he would imminently be relieved of his duties.

The classy statement follows Carrick former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that he had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of his dismissal.

Neville told Sky Sports News: 'In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

In a recent development, 'It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued.

'The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.

'I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all.'.

Less than an hour prior to Carrick's statement United confirmed his replacement, Pochettino, will take the reins after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the US’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his fresh job as United boss on Wednesday.

His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week due to his remaining contracted to US Soccer.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

Sources indicate that ‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’.

  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

In a recent development, “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Industry observers note that palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

Industry observers note that when it was declared Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

According to recent reports, "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Industry observers note that chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Industry observers note that palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Sources indicate that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, remarked. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

In a recent development, reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who remarked: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

In a recent development, any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Recent findings suggest that valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

In a recent development, on the defeat by Chelsea, Farke noted: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

According to recent reports, “All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

It has been revealed that but inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

In a recent development, estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke stated: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In a recent development, in Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate upcoming players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

It has been revealed that nel corso del consueto appuntamento con il video aggiornamento sul suo canale YouTube, Fabrizio Romano ha fatto il punto sul calciomercato in entrata del Milan soffermandosi in modo particolare sul nome di Gonçalo Inacio. Di seguito le sue dichiarazioni:.

"Teniamolo lì il nome di Gonçalo Inacio. Anche dal Portogallo sono arrivate conferme a quanto vi abbiamo raccontato, cioè che Inacio può essere un protagonista del mercato di gennaio. Io vi ribadisco quello che vi racconto da mesi, in realtà, ovvero i rapporti, perché l'agente Miguel Pino è lo stesso agente di Ruben Amorim. Sono tutti portoghesi, Amorim ha allento Inacio allo Sporting. Arrivare a gennaio comunque non è semplice, significa essere pronti ad essere buttati nel fuoco. Non sempre è semplice. Prendere Gonçalo Inacio significherebbe per Amorim prendere un ragazzo che conosce, con cui parla la stessa lingua, non solo verbale ma anche di campo. C'è un feeling diverso, non dovrebbe spiegare nulla al ragazzo. Il Milan sta tenendo attivi i contatti con il giocatore, la sua partenza a gennaio è possibile, le porte sono eventualmente aperto. Poi bisogna capire le condizioni, i prezzi, è chiaro che il Milan non si fa prendere soltanto dalla voglia di regalarsi un giocatore così per un prezzo qualsiasi. Bisognerà negoziare, ed anzi, la scorsa estate il Milan tra gli alti e i bassi di questa trattativa a un certo punto sperava di poter strappare una formula che potesse essere un prestito anche molto oneroso con diritto di riscatto per facilitare il tutto dal punto di vista economico. Il Milan ha più nomi in lista, ma quello di Inacio va preso assolutamente in considerazione".

Sources indicate that al podcast Passa dal BSMT di Gianluca Gazzoli, l’ex difensore Lele Adani ha parlato anche della fine della Bobo TV. “Qualcosa che mi manca del periodo della Bobo TV? Sono cose anche vecchie ormai, no? Fino a quel momento della rottura comunque lo ricordo e sono grato di averlo vissuto. Chiaramente da quando ci siamo separati, ma sono anche quasi contento che si sia fermato, dico che è meglio così.

La cosa importante della vita è che prima di tutto ti cresce. Io ne avrei fatto a meno sempre e credo tutti, ma ti cresce, ti forma, ti fa vedere le cose in un altro modo. Ma io non cambierei nulla. Io lo ritornerei a vivere il mio rapporto nello stesso modo, è stato troppo bello, ma meno male che si è fermato e sono molto più felice ora.

Industry observers note that riunirsi come gli Oasis? Dal mio punto di vista, credo che neanche se ne parlerà, è una cosa archiviata per sempre. Torno a dirlo: auguro il meglio io, non si vive di rancore per com’è andata, padre tempo opera sempre in silenzio. Ma sempre spererò che tutto vada per il meglio a tutti gli interpreti. Senza portare rancore, ma con la fermezza e la consapevolezza che non ci sarà più quel tempo”.

According to recent reports, kenneth Taylor è diventato in pochi mesi il perno insostituibile del centrocampo della Lazio di Gennaro Gattuso, attirando inevitabilmente le attenzioni dei principali club europei. Arrivato dieci mesi fa dall'Ajax per una cifra inferiore ai 17 milioni di euro, il 24enne ha completato una trasformazione e da semplice mezzala si è evoluto in un regista aggiunto che detta i tempi, accompagna la manovra e garantisce equilibrio. Adesso, secondo quanto rivelato da TuttoSport, la Juventus intende preparare un assalto invernale da circa 40 milioni di euro, affiancandosi ai sondaggi dalla Premier League di Brentford, Newcastle e Bournemouth.

It has been revealed that nonostante l'evidente attrattiva economica dell'operazione - che frutterebbe una plusvalenza considerevole pur dovendo riconoscere il 10% sulla rivendita all'Ajax - il presidente Claudio Lotito e il direttore sportivo Angelo Fabiani hanno infatti blindato i gioielli della rosa in vista di gennaio, respingendo al mittente tanto gli approcci per Taylor. Come anche la proposta da 25 milioni del Brentford per Gustav Isaksen. A blindare ulteriormente la permanenza nella Capitale è stato lo stesso centrocampista olandese, che ha già rassicurato Gattuso sulla ferma volontà di restare a Roma almeno fino al termine della stagione per dare seguito insieme ai sogni d'alta classifica.

It has been revealed that il "no" della Lazio è netto, ma la Juventus è già pronta a virare sulle alternative individuate alla Continassa per soddisfare le richieste di Luciano Spalletti. Per l'immediato, il primo nome in cima alla lista è quello di Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg: il trentunenne centrocampista danese è in uscita dall'Olympique Marsiglia e vede di buon grado una nuova sfida in Serie A, dove la sua esperienza internazionale e la qualità in regia porterebbero subito peso specifico alla mediana bianconera. Parallelamente, in prospettiva futura, resta viva l'opzione legata al giovane talento Darryl Bakola, per il quale i bianconeri dovranno però superare la ricca concorrenza inglese e la resistenza del Sassuolo. In questo senso l'ex CEO neroverde Giovanni Carnevali avrebbe in serbo un'offerta.

Industry News: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s latest-look midfield

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick remarked. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

It has been revealed that united probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Recent findings suggest that carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game blueprint.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Sources indicate that mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick mentioned. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s newly introduced-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

It has been revealed that carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick mentioned. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

In a recent development, michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

Industry observers note that it must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Industry observers note that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick remarked. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

In a recent development, “I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the upcoming challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

It has been revealed that sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

Marco Brescianini e Denis Man sono due profili sondati da Fabiani per la Lazio, mentre resta da chiarire se il club potrà operare nel mercato di gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Lottomatica, Lotito sta lavorando a un piano economico-finanziario che permetta al direttore sportivo di cercare rinforzi per Gattuso, secondo quanto riferisce Lottomatica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that fino a qualche settimana fa, il blocco del mercato sembrava quasi certo. Lotito punta però a ottenere il via libera della Commissione indipendente, che ha preso il posto della Covisoc.

Tra le operazioni su cui lavora ci sono l’anticipo dei crediti futuri legati alle sponsorizzazioni e una proroga per dilazionare il pagamento delle vecchie imposte relative agli anni del Covid. Dall’esito di questo lavoro dipende la possibilità per Fabiani di intervenire a gennaio.

According to recent reports, nel frattempo, Fabiani sta valutando diversi calciatori. Uno dei nomi indicati è Marco Brescianini, che la fonte presenta come giocatore di proprietà della Fiorentina. Gattuso lo apprezza soprattutto per la capacità di inserirsi in area di rigore.

L’operazione non viene considerata semplice. La Lazio può comunque contare su un elemento nei rapporti per un’eventuale trattativa: Brescianini ha lo stesso agente di Pinamonti.

It has been revealed that quello del rinnovo di Marcus Thuram sarà uno degli argomenti più caldi dei prossimi mesi in casa Inter. L'attaccante francese, infatti, avrebbe chiesto uno stipendio più alto rispetto ai sei milioni di euro percepiti attualmente. La Gazzetta dello Sport prova a tracciare un possibile scenario:.

"Proviamo a immaginare: Thuram rinnova per tre stagioni, fino al 2031, accettando di scendere a una base media di 5 milioni più succulenti premi declinati in varie specialità: il traguardo degli 8 in un’unica stagione si raggiungerebbe, per esempio, se il giocatore chiudesse in doppia cifra per gol e assist e se, contemporaneamente, la squadra vincesse lo scudetto e centrasse gli ottavi di Champions".

"E’ solo un gioco, naturalmente, per spiegare le strategie della società. Che risparmierebbe comunque sullo stipendio lordo, grazie al famoso decreto crescita, ma non può aumentare il tetto stipendi per mantenere l’equilibrio finanziario: vale per Thuram, come per Calhanoglu e per tutti gli altri. Solo Pio ha ricevuto un robusto adeguamento, anzi ha praticamente triplicato i guadagni. Ma nel suo caso si è trattato di un investimento a lunga scadenza, fino al 2032, per un ragazzo di 21 anni. L’età conta nel calcio moderno quasi quanto la qualità".

(Fonte: La Gazzetta dello Sport).

'I was one day away from falling into a coma': JAKE O'BRIEN, the Premier League's only diabetic player, on his brush with death, managing his condition in the dressing room - and why he was 'never close' to leaving Everton last summer

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1568 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • There are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door.
  • But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026.

There are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door. So you can imagine the reaction Jake O’Brien received when he pulled out his mobile just before one half-time team talk.

But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.

O’Brien’s body is unable to create insulin, the hormone that regulates the amount of glucose in your blood.

Recent findings suggest that loaded on his mobile is an app linked via Bluetooth to a circular device on his arm which gives a reading of his blood sugar levels. It is then that he takes out a needle and injects the necessary insulin dose into his thigh or stomach.

‘There was one guy who didn’t react too well. Mentioning no names! He was saying: "What are you doing on your phone?"' O’Brien recalls. ‘But he soon realised what it was for.’.

It can also come as a shock to the uninitiated among his team-mates.

‘One or two are taken aback at first,’ he says. ‘It can be a bit confusing. “What’s he doing?’’ Or maybe those that are a little squeamish, but they soon get used to it. It's only a small needle.'.

Everton and Ireland defender Jake O'Brien is the only diabetic footballer in the Premier League.

O'Brien (pictured attending an awareness workshop put on by Everton) revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador.

O'Brien (pictured with his partner Sophie) claims some of his team-mates are 'taken aback' when he injects himself with insulin (Source: Instagram/Obrienjake_).

Tracking blood glucose levels is now an everyday part of O'Brien's life but it is a life that was unwittingly put in jeopardy prior to his diagnosis at 16.

O’Brien was later told he had been just one day away from slipping into a coma when his concerned parents ushered him to the doctors near the family home in Youghal, County Cork, for a check-up.

Their sports-mad son, who had won national titles at boxing and hurling, was tired, losing weight and had an insatiable thirst despite drinking eight to nine litres of water a day. He had lost seven kilograms in just over a week. A blood test revealed his blood sugar was ten times what was considered stable and he was rushed to hospital.

‘I was told I was a day away from a coma,' indicates O'Brien. 'If I had gone to sleep that night without having gone to the doctor, who knows?’.

He went into hospital that night weighing 53kg, or just over eight stone. Two weeks post-diagnosis he was back up to 60kg, and within two years he had put on a whopping 30kg.

'Yeah, 30kg,' laughs O'Brien. 'I know it's not normal. It must have been some grocery bill for Mum, but I was motivated to put on the weight, going to the gym all the time.

‘I was a bit naive about it all,' he deadpans. ‘I never expected to have anything but once I knew what diabetes was, I didn’t wallow in it, I took it as a positive. Everything just clicked for me physically. I just thought, "Right, now I know what’s wrong, I can get on with my life again".

‘It was a pain going in and out of hospital, but I just took it as education and wanted to get my sport back on track.

'My family are... I wouldn't say cold, but matter of fact. Supportive, obviously, but they are all sporty too, so it was just, "Get on with it".'.

O'Brien's life in the Premier League would have seemed inconceivable when he fell down to 53kg as a teenager and was hospitalised.

Sources indicate that he is now an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

Today, relaxing in the cafe at Everton’s Finch Farm training complex, O’Brien is an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

There’s a Cork-lilt to his softly spoken Irish tone. He’s polite and engaging and it’s clear he revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador, spreading the message that diagnosis doesn’t have to end your dreams.

Such has been his impact, he has even attracted support from fans of the other club in the city.

One, six-year-old Liverpool fan Louis, reached out via Instagram to ask O’Brien how he kept up his glucose levels during a game and whether he suffered any ‘hypos’ - the expression for hypoglycemic episodes, when the blood sugar drops too low and leaves you faint or dizzy.

It has been revealed that louis, whose siblings Paisley and Evie also have Type One diabetes, followed up by challenging O’Brien to a penalty shootout. If the Everton man lost, he faced a forfeit, he would have to shout ‘Up the Reds’ on social media.

‘You play for the wrong team but you're still a Type One hero, and Mum states you're proof that diabetes doesn't stop you from playing at the top level,’ posted Louis.

Touched by the message, O’Brien asked Everton to invite the youngster and his family to training for a kickabout, although ultimately, we are assured they reached a compromise on the penalties forfeit.

Industry observers note that ‘I’ve struck up a rapport with some kids and groups here and in Ireland,' indicates O'Brien. 'They often have the same story as mine of not being sure what the future holds.

‘There’s a massive misconception about diabetes over what it is and the limitations it brings.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over.’.

Industry observers note that ‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel. I may inject four times before a night game and a bit more at half-time'.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over,’ claims O'Brien, who also excelled at boxing and hurling as a boy (Source: TikTok/Everton).

The centre back credits boxing for helping discipline with his diet but underlines ‘no food is off limits, it’s just about applying common sense'.

Industry observers note that A typical day sees him eat eggs, salmon and dates for breakfast to match his insulin doses to the carbohydrates he’s taking on around 9.30am before training. Afterwards he’ll have a light lunch at 2pm then take something back from the training ground for a light evening meal.

Industry observers note that ‘I just have to watch carbohydrates. I’ll eat more of them on match day but then work out my insulin ratio to the amount I eat and whether I need to inject more.

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel, I may inject four times before a night game and inject a bit more at half-time. If it’s not quite right you may get a bit heavy-legged or if I get a few cramps I may need a gel. But I've had no dangerous episodes.'.

When World Diabetes Day dawns on Saturday, O’Brien will be fully focused on preparing to play for Ireland in Austria in the Nations League.

It will give him a chance to revert to his favoured centre back position having been asked to fill in predominantly at right back under David Moyes.

He acknowledges it's not his preferred role but dismisses rumours that he wanted to leave as a result in the summer.

In a recent development, 'There was nothing in that,' O'Brien affirms. ‘I was never close to leaving.

Recent findings suggest that 'People know I'm not a natural right back but I'll play wherever I need to, to help the team. We're only a small squad so it’s crucial everyone chips in.

According to recent reports, ‘There’s a lot of different right backs. I see Arsenal have centre backs playing at right back so I can take pointers from them but then again, I am 6ft 6in so I’m not the average shape.’.

O'Brien insists there was 'nothing in' reports that he wanted to leave Everton last summer to get more minutes at his preferred position of centre back.

At least O’Brien has former Everton captain Seamus Coleman on hand for advice.

It has been revealed that ‘Seamus is a good friend. He still gives me pointers of where to be, positioning wise and seeing the game differently.'.

Ireland assistant John O'Shea, a versatile defender himself in his Manchester United days, is another mentor. O’Shea and Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson were at Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch O'Brien play his part in Everton's recent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

Recent findings suggest that 'Heimir is a good guy,' says O'Brien. 'Very understanding. It's always a nice change of scenery to link up with Ireland. We've got a difficult couple of games (Austria and Kosovo) but hopefully if we get two wins it’s within reach.'.

Indeed, if there's a mantra that personifies O'Brien's outlook on life, no matter what knocks you take, it is: always believe you can still achieve.

'Don’t be afraid and don’t let anything hold you back, that's what I say.'.

Il PSV lo ha acquistato pochi mesi fa dall'AZ Alkmaar per 13 milioni di euro, ma oggi il valore di Sven Mijnans è già almeno raddoppiato. Bologna, Fiorentina, Roma, Lazio, Milan e Napoli hanno seguito in tempi diversi il centrocampista offensivo classe 2000, protagonista di un avvio di stagione straordinario che lo ha definitivamente consacrato tra i migliori interpreti del ruolo in Eredivisie.

Industry observers note that I numeri parlano da soli. In campionato ha già messo insieme 9 gol e 2 assist nelle prime 10 giornate, confermando una crescita costante anche sotto il profilo realizzativo. Nella scorsa stagione aveva chiuso con 21 reti in 50 presenze, di cui 11 in Eredivisie e 6 in Conference League, dopo le 11 segnate nell'annata precedente.

Industry observers note that mijnans è uno dei giocatori più decisivi del PSV, ma il suo valore va ben oltre le statistiche. Colpiscono soprattutto la capacità di leggere la partita in anticipo e l'intelligenza nei movimenti; sa abbassarsi per partecipare alla costruzione dell'azione, ma anche inserirsi tra le linee nel momento giusto, offrendo sempre una soluzione ai compagni e dando ritmo alla manovra. La sua mentalità è spiccatamente offensiva (ricorda un po' Reijnders) e, quando recupera il pallone, la prima scelta è quasi sempre quella di verticalizzare, cercando subito di mettere in difficoltà la difesa avversaria senza ricorrere a tocchi superflui.

Tra le qualità che attirano le major italiane c'è anche l'ottima tecnica sui calci piazzati: punizioni e corner rappresentano un'arma in più nel suo repertorio. A 26 anni Mijnans sta vivendo il momento migliore della carriera e abbina ormai maturità tattica e continuità di rendimento. Il passaggio dalla Eredivisie alla Serie A comporterebbe inevitabilmente un aumento del livello fisico e dell'intensità difensiva, ma le sue letture di gioco, la qualità tecnica e la capacità di incidere sia in rifinitura sia in zona gol spiegano perché soprattutto il Napoli stia valutando un investimento.

Mauricio Pochettino è pronto a introdurre una novità senza precedenti nella storia del Manchester United. Nel suo nuovo staff tecnico, infatti, ci sarà anche una donna: si tratta di Silvia Tuyà Viñas, preparatrice atletica spagnola di 46 anni, che diventerà la prima professionista a far parte di un gruppo di lavoro dei Red Devils.

In a recent development, per Tuyà Viñas non sarà però una prima assoluta al fianco dell'allenatore argentino. Nell'ottobre 2024 era entrata nello staff della Nazionale statunitense guidata da Pochettino, diventando anche in quel caso la prima donna inserita ufficialmente nello staff tecnico della selezione americana. Laureata e dottore di ricerca in Scienze dell'attività fisica e dello sport, la specialista vanta una preparazione accademica di alto livello e parla inglese, spagnolo e catalano, un aspetto che faciliterà il suo inserimento in un ambiente internazionale come quello dello United. Il suo percorso è iniziato in un centro di alto rendimento a Barcellona, prima delle prime esperienze nel calcio con il Levante Las Planas nella stagione 2018/19.

Il legame con Pochettino affonda le radici nell'esperienza del tecnico al Chelsea. In quel periodo Tuyà Viñas e il suo mentore Gerard Moras Feliu avevano collaborato come consulenti esterni per offrire una prospettiva diversa sulla metodologia di preparazione fisica dei Blues. A Manchester lavorerà insieme agli storici collaboratori di Pochettino: Jesús Pérez, Miguel D'Agostino e Toni Jiménez, oltre al figlio del tecnico, Sebastiano Pochettino, che continuerà il suo ruolo di responsabile della preparazione scientifica.
