Harry Kane had to compose himself and hold back the tears while reading beautiful letters from his children after breaking the England appearance record.

The 33-year-old earned his 126th cap and scored in the 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday night, with the Wembley crowd celebrating his achievement and Ballon d'Or triumph.

And on the following morning, there was a surprise in store for the England skipper, who was visibly taken aback on camera when presented with letters from his four children, nine-year-old Ivy, eight-year-old Vivi, five-year-old Louis and three-year-old Henry, who he shares with wife Kate.

'Wow, that’s uh a bit of a surprise,' Kane mentioned as he examined the letters and artwork. 'I think you guys are trying to make me cry on camera.'.

He opened the first one before reading aloud: 'To Daddy, I love you very much and I want you to know that I’m very proud of you and also you are the best footballer in the world, the most kind Daddy in the world and the best striker in the world.

'I would like to celebrate you playing the most games for England by holiday together and eating ice cream.

Harry Kane was on the verge of tears as he read touching letters from his four children.

Industry observers note that 'My favorite thing about you is you never give up and I love all things you do for us. Love Ivy.'.

Dewy-eyed Kane then reflected: 'I wasn’t expecting this beautiful letter. Thank you Ivy. I love you. I've got one here from Vivian as well.'.

'Dear Daddy, I’m so happy and proud of you. I love you because you are hard working and make the best fried eggs. I want to celebrate with you by going fishing, going down the water slides and having a cinema trip as well. Love from Vivi.'.

Kane then remarked: 'Yeah, you’ve caught me by surprise here to be honest with you. I’m trying to just uh, stay strong for the camera. Thank you Vivi, love you.'.

Then came the letters from Kane's two sons, Louis and Henry.

Louis' read: 'To Daddy, I love you so much because you train and work so hard. My favorite thing we do together is play football and cricket together. I love when you play England football because you score goals and we get to sing Vindaloo. I want to celebrate with you by making an ice cream house with sweets inside. Love Louis.'.

In a recent development, 'Thank you Louie, love you, boy. This last one is from Henry,' Kane mentioned.

It has been revealed that the short and sweet note from his youngest went: 'Daddy, you are the winner. Vindaloo! Love Henry.'.

Kane walked onto the pitch with his children, (L-R) Henry, Ivy, Vivi, Louis on Thursday night.

Kane showed the artwork and hand-written letters to the camera as he read them.

Kane then pointed the endearing scribble to the camera, saying: 'He’s drawn me a lovely picture there. Love you, Henry. Thank you, beautiful messages from my wonderful family.'.

Kane, who lives with his family in Bavaria and recently signed a fresh deal worth £400,000-a-week at Bayern Munich, brought the whole clan, including his parents, to Wembley for his significant night on Thursday.

He walked out onto the hallowed turf with his four children, admired a gigantic tifo of himself in the crowd, posed for pictures with the gleaming Ballon d'Or trophy and was given a commemorative shirt by Prince William.

Kane is a devoted family man in addition to being the world's best footballer and took a moment to say a few words about his children at the Ballon d'Or ceremony last month.

He remarked: 'To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

Prince William presented Kane with a commemorative framed shirt with 126 on the back.

In a recent development, 'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'.

Kane passed Peter Shilton as the record appearance-maker for England on Thursday and took his tally of goals for the national team to 92.

In a recent development, his penalty put England 2-1 up and they would not relinquish their lead. He'll next be in action against Spain on Sunday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso noted: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

In a recent development, “It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

It has been revealed that asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very key part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a significant topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

Industry observers note that this is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the glitch yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Sources indicate that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Recent findings suggest that defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury promptly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

In a recent development, none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is at the moment on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

According to recent reports, it is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a upcoming reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he stated. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Recent findings suggest that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

According to recent reports, chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

According to recent reports, belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

Sources indicate that we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

According to recent reports, there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

In a recent development, fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

According to recent reports, you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Sources indicate that liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

Industry observers note that this game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Sources indicate that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Sources indicate that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a upcoming left-back in due course.

Recent findings suggest that so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

In a recent development, palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

Industry observers note that one way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

Recent findings suggest that that’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

Industry observers note that that’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

According to recent reports, there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

It has been revealed that A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

It has been revealed that austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Recent findings suggest that wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Sources indicate that xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

Recent findings suggest that we are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a significant buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

In a recent development, will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Industry observers note that dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ.

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

In a recent development, hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

In a recent development, we know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a substantial game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a upcoming chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

Recent findings suggest that there have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures upcoming in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Sources indicate that glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

Ne abbiamo parlato lungamente anche nell'editoriale: Gustavo Varela, straordinariamente capocannoniere della Serie A con 9 reti in 10 partite giocate, è un giocatore già da grande squadra? Non ha esperienza, non ha trascorsi in una big e di fatto è in un campionato top da poche partite. Possibile che valga già 40 milioni di euro?

Ne parliamo nel Podcast di oggi di Tuttomercatoweb.com in compagnia di Marco Conterio.

Arrivato al Monza dal Benfica per circa 3,5 milioni di euro, ha messo insieme 9 gol in Serie A e 2 in Coppa Italia, conquistando anche la prima convocazione in Nazionale. Numeri che hanno acceso l'interesse delle massive: il Napoli si è mosso per primo, con Giovanni Manna che ha incontrato l'agente Hector Paris, mentre anche la Juventus ha sondato il terreno. Dall'Inghilterra seguono la situazione Tottenham, Brighton, Brentford, Sunderland e Liverpool, con quest'ultimo che avrebbe inviato osservatori a visionarlo. Il Monza valuta il proprio gioiello tra i 35 e i 40 milioni di euro e vorrebbe trattenerlo almeno fino al termine della stagione. Attenzione però al Benfica, che conserva il 20% sulla futura rivendita e il diritto di pareggiare le eventuali offerte. Ma vale già una cifra del genere?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Un po' meno quest'anno perché non ho cambiato tanti ruoli, anche se posso farlo.
  • Sources indicate that che cosa ha visto in te Amorim?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that il centrocampista del Milan Yunus Musah è stato intervistato in esclusiva dai colleghi di SportMediaset. Di seguito le sue dichiarazioni.

Ti senti il jolly del Milan? "Un po' meno quest'anno perché non ho cambiato tanti ruoli, anche se posso farlo. Ho potuto giocare a centrocampo e migliorare in questo aspetto".

Sources indicate that che cosa ha visto in te Amorim? "Penso che ha visto le mie partite vecchie, perché già sapeva cosa si aspettasse da me e cosa mi poteva chiedere. Ha fatto i suoi doveri, ha guardato tutto, e sapeva già cosa e come poteva sfruttarmi".

Non ti abbiamo mai visto giocare terzino sinistro al Milan come a Genova: come è nata questa idea? "Non lo so (ride, ndr). Questa domanda è per il mister. Bartesaghi ed Estupinan sono molto forti, ma lui quel giorno voleva un destro sulla sinistra".

Recent findings suggest that dipendesse da te: dove ti vedi? "Penso giocando a centrocampo. Non fisso però, potendo andare un po' ovunque così che posso prendere la palla, abbassarmi, senza essere fisso".

Secondo te sta crescendo il Milan? È possibile lo Scudetto? "È possibile. Ci alleniamo ogni giorno per questo. Abbiamo tutti il sogno e l'ambizione di vincerlo, e faremo il possibile per arrivare fino in fondo".

In a recent development, ci racconti cosa ti ricordi del tuo periodo negli States? "Niente (ride, ndr)".

Recent findings suggest that cosa ti è rimasto dell'America? "Giocare per gli Stati Uniti mi ha aiutato ad avere questo senso di appartenenza. Fino ai 17 anni avevo solo il passaporto, ma adesso mi sento parte della cultura".

It has been revealed that in cosa ti senti americano? "Posso andare lì, conosco i ristoranti, le catene, le persone dei diversi Stati, la geografia. Capisco tanto la gente americana adesso".

Ti senti il cuore a stelle e strisce "Ho tanti passaporti, ho vissuto e cresciuto in tanti paesi, come qui in Italia, in Inghilterra, quindi mi sento un po' di tutto".

Sei mai tornato a vedere i tuoi posti di infanzia? "Si nel 2021 sono tornato a New York, ho visto la casa dove ho vissuto quell'anno. Il Bronx, è stato bello vederlo. C'era un pezzo che mancava nella mia memoria, ed è stato bello poterlo collegare".

È vero che hai un gatto che si chiama Bronx? "Si. L'ho lasciato con i vicini a Valencia perché non ho potuto portarlo a Milano".

Dall'America la tua famiglia si trasferisce in Italia "Già era in Italia la mia famiglia, e mia mamma doveva fare avanti e indietro in America".

According to recent reports, com'è stata la tua infanzia a Castelfranco Veneto? "Bellissima. È un posto dove i miei genitori non avevano paura di lasciarmi giocare tutto il giorno fuori al parcheggio vicino al condominio di casa".

È vero che sono stati anni di sacrifici economici quelli dei tuoi genitori? "Certo. Ovviamente quando sono cresciuto non eravamo ricchi, non avevamo tanti soldi, ma da quando ho lasciato casa, ma anche quando ero piccolo, i miei genitori non mi hanno mai fatto mancare niente. Spero di essere il loro orgoglio, perché loro sono il mio".

Arsenal e Valencia: sei un esploratore del mondo. Che passaggi sono stati? "Giocare per l'Arsenal è stato un grande privilegio, perché sono arrivato dall'Italia a 9 anni, ho giocato con una squadretta e sono subito passato all'Arsenal. Ero pronto per passare in prima squadra arrivato ai 16 anni, e il Valencia aveva un progetto per me. Ho vissuto 4 anni bellissimi in Spagna, è una città che resterà sempre nel mio cuore".

Industry observers note that che aria si respira nello spogliatoio? "L'anno scorso guardavo tanto, era una squadra molto solida e difficile da battere. Amorim ha portato un'aria molto positiva, ci capiamo. Lui capisce molto il giocatore e viceversa. Aiuta quando capisce di cosa hanno bisogno i giocatori, lui è bravo in queste cose, e i giocatori in squadra sono abbastanza tranquilli".

Però è uno che quando c'è bisogno si arrabbia "Si. Dopo il Ferencvaros era molto arrabbiato, come tutti".

Sources indicate that che legami ai con l'Africa? "Mia moglie è del Zanzibar, la mia famiglia ghanese. Quindi è bello fare viaggi in estate nei nostri paesi d'origine".

Lotito e Fabiani conoscono dal 15 novembre la cifra da coprire; resta il nodo della liquidità per gli acquisti.

La Lazio può ancora evitare il blocco totale del mercato invernale. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani conoscono dal 15 novembre la cifra da coprire, ma non hanno ancora consegnato i documenti alla Commissione di controllo. Il termine è il 30 novembre; l’organismo li esaminerà a dicembre. Anche un eventuale via libera, però, non garantirebbe alla società la liquidità necessaria per acquistare senza vendere giocatori importanti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, gli acquisti estivi e l’aumento degli ingaggi hanno peggiorato l’indice del Costo del lavoro allargato, portandolo oltre il limite previsto per operare a saldo zero. Lotito lavora da mesi per rientrare attraverso crediti futuri e altri asset. Potrebbe inoltre intervenire successivamente con un’immissione di denaro, così da scongiurare il blocco e mantenere la libertà di operare sul mercato.

In a recent development, il passaggio immediato resta la presentazione della documentazione entro il 30 novembre. fino a questo momento non è stata consegnata alla Commissione, chiamata a valutarla nel mese di dicembre.

Superare il limite consentirebbe alla Lazio di entrare nel mercato, ma la possibilità di operare non coinciderebbe necessariamente con quella di comprare. Anche ottenendo il via libera, il club potrebbe non disporre della liquidità per effettuare acquisti senza cedere pezzi da novanta.

Sources indicate that su questo punto si concentrerà il prossimo vertice con Gattuso. Sarà l’allenatore a indicare la strada, tenendo conto sia dei margini di mercato sia della possibilità di conservare la rosa attuale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:58 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:57 EST, 13 November 2026.

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Industry observers note that six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and  endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year.

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers.

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

They were punished 'for violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl'.

Recent findings suggest that dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

He noted: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'.

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

Sources indicate that 'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?".

Recent findings suggest that 'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'.

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'.

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was quickly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man remarked a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview.

He stated in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

Industry observers note that 'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'.

Industry observers note that his companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'.

In a recent development, dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

Sources indicate that 'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'.

E’ andato in scena la prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, riconoscimento dedicato alle figure che hanno lasciato il segno nel panorama calcistico nazionale. Tra i vincitori figura anche il vicepresidente della SSC Napoli, Edoardo De Laurentiis, premiato per i meriti conseguiti nell’area della Governance: “E’ per me un grande onore ricevere questo riconoscimento, ma la gioia è doppia per averlo condiviso con mio padre, che è il mio mentore e la mia guida. Ho mosso i primi passi in questo mondo quando ero ancora molto giovane, ho commesso diversi sbagli, ma mi impegno quotidiano per crescere ed essere all’altezza del mio ruolo”.

In a recent development, successivamente, a margine della cerimonia di premiazione, il vicepresidente ha aggiunto: “La chiave è proseguire giorno dopo giorno con costanza, facendo gruppo. La coesione è fondamentale per raggiungere gli obiettivi prefissati. Diventerà la futura casa del Napoli (riferendosi al nuovo centro sportivo), un luogo in cui far crescere i giovani, costruire il nostro vivaio e scoprire nuovi talenti. Abbiamo vissuto tantissime esperienze entusiasmanti, dall’era Spalletti fino a Conte. La più grande è stata osservare la squadra capace di conquistare costantemente traguardi prestigiosi e di mantenersi sempre ad altissimi livelli”.

According to recent reports, "Il Milan secondo me ora non deve guardare la classifica ma il percorso. Pensare adesso alla conquista di un posto in Champions League potrebbe essere controproducente. Il marchio calcistico d’impostazione di Amorim è evidente, le potenzialità della squadra sono in crescita. La parola d’ordine è ora continuità. Adesso si deve pretendere di più sia dall’allenatore sia dalla squadra, anche perché vedo il presidente Gerry Cardinale carico e vicino alla squadra come forse mai. L’ho “respirato” da vicino prima del derby, è pieno di passione e ambizione e si è letteralmente esaltato con quella vittoria. La squadra aveva bisogno di sentirlo cosi vicino e lui aveva bisogno di vivere momenti così in prima persona. Sono curioso di vedere quali saranno i suoi prossimi colpi".

Recent findings suggest that la sosta è ormai un lontano ricordo, e la Serie B è pronta a tornare in campo, con la 12ª giornata del campionato che prenderà il via questa sera per concludersi poi nel pomeriggio di domenica (CLICCA QUI per leggere il programma completo del turno). Dieci gare in tutto, e tutte molto interessanti, da seguire anche attraverso i nostri live match, ma andiamo a vedere ora le tre che - per i più svariati motivi - possono rubare maggiormente la scena alle altre.

It has been revealed that ascoli-Vicenza: dopo un periodo decisamente no, i veneti hanno comunque confermato Fabio Gallo, che è però chiamato alla svolta abbastanza immediata. I marchigiani, però, non sono certo l'avversario più abbordabile, da neo promossi sono ora terzi. Ed ecco, proprio quest'ultimo dettaglio accomuna le due compagini: il Vicenza ha stravinto il campionato di C il 16 marzo, l'Ascoli è dovuto passare dai playoff; poi tutto è cambiato. Si vede adesso la truppa bianconera solida ed equilibrata, più vulnerabile il 3-5-2 dei biancorossi.

Catanzaro-Palermo: aquile a un passo dalla A nella passata stagione, siciliani che puntano dritto a quell'obiettivo da primi in classifica. Momento invece opposto per i calabresi, fanalino di coda della graduatoria cadetta, che dovranno mettere in campo adesso le migliorie richieste da Mignani: battere la capolista, imbattuta, potrebbe svoltare la stagione. La speranza, sponda giallorossa, potrebbe aumentare per il fatto che, tra le mura amiche, il gol è sempre arrivato; si dovrà però non subirne.

Empoli-Pisa: società unite sull'assurdità di un divieto di trasferta, definito mediante una nota ufficiale come "sconfitta" del calcio, ma in campo sarà battaglia, perché gli azzurri non hanno ancora trovato continuità e cambio di passo dopo l'arrivo di Andreoletti in panchina, i nerazzurri non vincono invece da quattro giornata. La vittoria, per nessuna delle due, può essere un'opzione. E i gol? Negli ultimi cinque incontri ufficiali non sono mancati...

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm.
  • Sources indicate that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.

They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

Sources indicate that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining aims and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

Recent findings suggest that the two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once manufacturer secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

According to recent reports, the venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends.

‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ said Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’.

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he mentioned: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’.

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’.

According to recent reports, ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

Industry observers note that ‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’.

Recent findings suggest that the traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ mentioned Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’.

Ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ stated Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’.

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a big role in its rise.

Industry observers note that riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’.

Riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’.

His tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ says Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

Industry observers note that the repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

In a recent development, the benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

In a recent development, ‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he said.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The issues you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’.

In a recent development, walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ noted Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’.

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

‘We need facts or what is called data,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country.

‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’.

Recent findings suggest that this is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie remarked: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’.

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player mentioned to another: “Good game, son”.’.

In a recent development, the football world has thus moved into a latest era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’.

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’.

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org.

Federico Gatti resta uno dei più chiacchierati in vista del mercato di gennaio. L'impiego ridotto all'osso in campionato (appena 183 minuti complessivi) impongono riflessioni sul futuro del centrale italiano. L'ultimo club che si è fatto avanti per il 28enne è stato la Lazio, spinta dall'emergenza difensiva provocata dall'infortunio di Josip Sutalo, destinato a restare ai box fino all'inizio di febbraio. Il direttore sportivo biancoceleste Angelo Fabiani ha già avviato i primi contatti esplorativi - secondo quanto rivelato da TuttoSport - con gli agenti Dario Paolillo e Luca Carnaghi per sondare la fattibilità di un trasferimento nella Capitale, dove il tecnico Gennaro Gattuso lo stima profondamente e gli garantirebbe quella maglia da titolare.

L'operazione presenta tuttavia ostacoli economici e strategici non trascurabili. Alla Continassa la valutazione del difensore italiano - legato ai bianconeri da un contratto fino al 2030 - resta fissata attorno ai 20 milioni di euro, una richiesta che già in estate aveva frenato le pretendenti e che difficilmente la Juventus abbasserà concedendo formule agevolate come il prestito con diritto di riscatto. A maggior ragione nei confronti di una diretta concorrente per la qualificazione in Champions League. Sebbene Gatti stia continuando a spingere al massimo in allenamento per provare a scalare nuovamente le gerarchie interne, le prossime settimane di campionato risulteranno decisive: senza un'inversione di tendenza sul piano del minutaggio, l'ipotesi di un addio invernale prenderà seriamente quota.

In a recent development, oltre al pressing biancoceleste, attorno al numero 4 juventino si muove infatti una folta concorrenza sia in Italia sia all'estero. In Serie A resta vigile il Napoli di Massimiliano Allegri e Giovanni Manna - che già in estate aveva messo Gatti in cima alla lista dei desideri prima di frenare per i costi - mentre oltreconfine non mancano gli estimatori tra club impegnati in Champions League come Porto e Galatasaray e diverse formazioni di Premier League, tra cui Everton, Sunderland e Nottingham Forest. Nonostante le sirene d'Oltremanica esercitino finora minor fascino sul difensore italiano rispetto a soluzioni di primo piano, il mercato invernale si preannuncia caldissimo per definire il futuro di uno dei profili più corteggiati della retroguardia bianconera.

If Spanish refs can speak up so can ours... over to you, Willie

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.
  • It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.

Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.

It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.

Back in August 2023, leading official John Beaton addressed calls for greater openness around VAR and gave the impression the refereeing firmament were in favour of a fresh spirit of glasnost.

‘Anything to explain how we are arriving at decisions and anything we can do to show people what we do on a Saturday and what happens in the VAR centre, we absolutely welcome,’ he said.

‘The more transparency, the better. The more questions we get, the more answers we can provide and, we hope, get to a better place,’.

That was followed by newly introduced head of refereeing Willie Collum’s VAR show on YouTube the following season. At that point, there seemed a real move to lift the lid and build confidence in our men in black. There was talk of Collum doing his programme more than once a month and suggestions referees might even be open to being interviewed post-match in the right circumstances.

Unfortunately, though, all that has come to nothing and last term — in which controversial decisions had a huge effect on the title race — feels like it could become an obstacle in the way of progress.

Head of Referees Willie Collum should be applauded for speaking up on the SFA VAR show.

It needn’t be, though. There has always been a feeling among referees that being put in front of the cameras carried danger. SFA Ian Maxwell has also spoken about the game being subject to ‘fairly hysterical commentary’ when something bad happens.

The media environment here is nowhere near as febrile as in Spain, though. It has four newspapers dedicated to sport alone. There are countless chat indicates on council telly full of talking heads. Ages ago, news bulletins there had lipreaders telling viewers what coaches and players were saying on the park. Jose Mourinho is also back ruffling officials’ feathers at Real Madrid.

Getting Spanish refs to a place where they feel ready to be interviewed has taken time. It has also taken extra cash for them from TV money and it can still go a lot further.

Industry observers note that A selected referee will speak to broadcast rights-holders only. And it’s not after every game. Only selected fixtures.

The SFA made real progress a couple of years back in lifting the curtain and should seek to rediscover that momentum — even though it won’t make the key problem of having to improve overall standards go away.

It has been revealed that since last year, the Spanish FA have been broadcasting their own YouTube show ‘Tiempo de Revision’ to address flashpoints. It should be noted that it’s inferior to Collum’s broadcast in terms of content.

It replays incidents against a musical backdrop with captions explaining the decisions. There is no in-game audio, no one like Collum putting himself out there.

Although some of his reasoning for major calls was a bit suspect last term, that programme remains a platform to build from.

Recent findings suggest that there is no reason why referees shouldn’t explain their decision-making after games here. Criticism they may or may not receive in the aftermath shouldn’t come into it.

If Spanish whistlers can go public, so can they.

Aurelio De Laurentiis, presidente del Napoli, è stato tra i protagonisti della prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, manifestazione dedicata alle personalità che si sono distinte nel panorama calcistico nazionale. L’evento si è svolto a Villa Campolieto, a Ercolano, dove il patron azzurro ha ricevuto un riconoscimento nella categoria Fair Play, che vedeva tra i finalisti anche Andrea Belotti e Luca Percassi. Nel corso del suo intervento, De Laurentiis ha parlato anche del film dedicato al Centenario del Napoli: “La sceneggiatura del film del centenario la scrive il qui presente Maurizio de Giovanni. Il calcio in Inghilterra è nato con gli aristocratici. Non era un fatto popolare. Arrivarono a Napoli e iniziarono a giocare con gli scugnizzi. Il 1922 sembrerebbe la vera data, poi procrastinata al 1926 per la nascita del Napoli. Che non si chiama Società Sportiva, ma Calcio Napoli. Questo film è venuto talmente bene che una piattaforma importante come Amazon lo porterà nel mondo. Quando abbiamo vinto lo Scudetto con Conte, ho fatto un film e sono andato a Los Angeles: presi questo cinema e ho fatto questa anteprima dove sono arrivati questi tifosi dall’America. C’erano donne emozionatissime che dicevano di non capire nulla di calcio ma che si sono comunque fatte trascinare. Ho scoperto che a San Pedro ci sono 30mila tifosi del Napoli legati all’isola d’Ischia”.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” indicates Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

In a recent development, “I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

It has been revealed that “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

Recent findings suggest that this game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

It has been revealed that alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

  • Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30.

Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

Despite Xabi Alonso acknowledging that the midfielder was carrying a fitness issue into the game at Sunderland before the November international break, Caicedo played the full 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light.

Prior to representing his country across two matches, the Blues star himself admitted that he was not fully fit, yet intended to feature in both games.

As well as playing 84 minutes against Costa Rica at the weekend, Caicedo featured for 45 minutes versus Bolivia on Tuesday night.

However, it has since been revealed that the 25-year-old requested to be withdrawn at half time.

Speaking to reporter Johanna Calderon after the Bolivia match, Caicedo suggested that he did not want to risk his fitness in the second half.

In an video posted on X, he remarked: "I wasn’t feeling too well, so I asked to come off.

"I have another commitment with my club, so I’m trying to get there as soon as possible and recover.".

Not only does Caicedo now face a long-haul flight from Ecuador, he is giving up five hours of recovery due to the time difference between Guayaquil and London.

When you factor in tiredness to add to the injury issue that he is presently trying to protect, Caicedo should not be starting the game with Leeds.

Jordan Henderson was not called up by England, whereas Romeo Lavia played on Sunday night having missed Belgium's first of two UEFA Nations game during the international break.

Starting that pair and having Caicedo on the substitutes' bench is the only scenario that makes sense for Alonso.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Per la trasferta del 28 novembre sono esauriti i 1.489 posti iniziali nel settore ospiti; restano altri tagliandi.

It has been revealed that per Lazio-Lecce sono attese 13.300 presenze all’Olimpico, il secondo dato stagionale più alto per una gara casalinga biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Corriere dello Sport, La vendita dei biglietti avanza lentamente, mentre il tifo organizzato conferma la protesta contro Lotito e la decisione di disertare le partite in casa.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that finora sono stati staccati circa 5.300 biglietti. A questi si aggiungono i 4.500 abbonati stagionali — una cifra non ufficializzata — e i 3.500 sostenitori che hanno aderito al Pack 3. Il totale provvisorio arriva così a 13.300 presenze, secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport.

In a recent development, il dato supera le 12.283 presenze registrate nell’ultima gara casalinga contro il Cagliari. Resta alle spalle soltanto delle 21.373 presenze contro il Milan, quando sugli spalti c’erano però circa 10.000 tifosi rossoneri.

L’affluenza resta lontana dalla normalità descritta per una squadra che guida da sola la classifica. Il tifo organizzato proseguirà infatti la contestazione a Lotito, nonostante i risultati ottenuti dalla formazione di Gattuso.

Recent findings suggest that il clima è diverso in vista del derby del 13 dicembre, indicato come l’unica eccezione alla protesta annunciata prima dell’inizio della stagione. Per la stracittadina sono già garantite 25.500 presenze, con la prospettiva di un Olimpico colorato di biancoceleste.

Recent findings suggest that la risposta alla prevendita è stata immediata nella seconda fase, riservata ai 29.918 abbonati della passata stagione. Il numero delle presenze garantite si avvicina a quella cifra; resta poi la fase aperta a tutti, che potrebbe portare il totale oltre quota 30.000.

It has been revealed that cresce anche l’attesa per la finale di Supercoppa italiana a San Siro. Il 23 novembre si aprirà la finestra di vendita riservata agli abbonati della stagione 2025-26. Al momento possono acquistare i biglietti soltanto gli abbonati al campionato in corso.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:58.

Chelsea have been handed a double injury boost ahead after Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino both represented Argentina on Tuesday night.

Martinez and Anselmino were called up by Lionel Scaloni despite spending weeks and months on the sidelines.

While goalkeeper Martinez had been unavailable with a fractured jaw since October 17, Anselmino has not played any competitive minutes for Chelsea in 2026-27 due to a hamstring injury.

However, the pair featured as Argentina cruised to a 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in Cordoba.

Starting between the sticks wearing a protective mask, Martinez played the full 90 minutes, albeit only having to make two saves during a one-sided contest.

Meanwhile, Anselmino was introduced as a 71st-minute substitute as the former world champions saw out the win.

Anselmino's outing - his first for Argentina - is particularly notable because it is his first since a 29-minute appearance in a pre-season friendly versus Johor DT on August 9.

When Moises Caicedo has provided a further fitness concern for Xabi Alonso, having Martinez and Anselmino come through unscathed for Argentina is a welcome boost.

Alonso must now decide whether to retain Mike Penders for Saturday's Premier League game with Leeds United or hand an immediate recall to Martinez.

Given the time difference and Penders having largely impressed in his absence, Martinez may expect to be named on the substitutes' bench.

Although it is possible that Anselmino will not feature in Chelsea's squad versus Leeds, Alonso requires an extra central-defensive option due to Maxence Lacroix being expected to be sidelined until January.

Realistically, the 21-year-old could be handed a start for the Blues' Under-21s ranks before coming into contention for the first team.
